title: Token-aligned cache-replay auditor and thresholded rollback advisor for prefix-cache anomalies
creator: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: We observe intermittent semantic deviations when requests hit the prefix/KV cache versus cold runs. Existing hit-conditioned probes measure delta at an aggregate level but lack token-aligned replay fidelity and a clear rollback decision boundary for rollouts. This ticket creates a lightweight auditor that (1) replays recorded requests with token-level alignment between cached and uncached runs, (2) computes semantic divergence metrics stratified by prompt shape and cache-hit pattern, and (3) outputs a thresholded rollback advisory signal used by canary gating. Goals: - Produce a reproducible replay harness that pins RNG/temperature and reproduces KV-hit sequences. - Compute token-aligned diffs (edit distance, embedding similarity per span, stop-token shifts) and a composite semantic-drift score. - Derive acceptance thresholds using historical canary data and false-positive controls. - Integrate advisory output with existing canary pipeline so rollbacks are triggered when score > threshold and sustained across N% of sampled requests. - Provide dashboards and a lightweight audit report for postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible replay harness exists that can run cached-vs-uncached comparisons with token alignment for a specified request set
Semantic-drift score is computed and documented; its components include token edit distance, per-span embedding similarity, and functional-output mismatches (e.g., JSON schema violations)
A thresholding strategy is implemented (auto-calibrated from historical canary runs) and exposed as a config parameter for rollout gates
Canary pipeline consumes the advisory and automatically pauses or rolls back a rollout when advisory conditions are met
Dashboards and a generated audit report (CSV + short HTML) are produced for each canary run and stored in the canary artifact bucket
steps: Instrument request recorder to capture inputs, model version, routing decisions, KV-hit map, and deterministic seeds
Implement replay harness that forces cache/no-cache runs with identical model config and captures token sequences and logits
Build token-aligned diff engine to compute: token edit distance, span alignments, per-span embedding cosine similarity, and stop-token shift count
Combine metrics into a composite semantic-drift score with tunable weights; add an option to ignore harmless formatting diffs
Calibrate thresholds by running the harness on past canary datasets and labeling known-good vs known-bad deployments
Expose advisory as an API consumed by the rollout controller with parameters: window_size, min_samples, score_threshold, persistence_required
Add a canary dashboard panel showing distribution of scores, example divergent pairs, and rollback triggers
Run end-to-end validation on staging and run a shadow canary alongside live rollouts for 2 full release cycles
comments: 2026-02-17 - Diego Morales: Spike complete. The replay harness can reproduce deterministic outputs for >95% of short prompts. Long multi-turn sequences need token freeze heuristics.
2026-02-22 - PM review (Samira Patel): Please ensure the advisor has adjustable sensitivity per-customer (enterprise workloads need lower false positives).
2026-03-01 - Design feedback (Luis Ortega): Add example UI for the canary dashboard showing exemplar diff pairs and confidence intervals.
2026-03-08 - Engineering note: Implemented embedding-based span similarity and small-variance normalization to avoid overfitting to tokenization noise.
2026-03-13 - Ops: Staging shadow canary ran for 24h against runtime-1.19 and flagged two rollbacks; both were reviewed and determined to be safe (false positives) — thresholds adjusted accordingly.
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on token-level alignment to catch cases where prefix hits move stop tokens or truncate generated JSON. We should avoid conflating harmless tokenization differences (e.g., whitespace) with real semantic regressions. Calibration will use historical labeled canary outcomes. Consider a follow-up that ties the advisory to per-customer tolerance profiles and automated canary playbook generation.
